topic: Function Template with Multiple Type Parameters and Operator Overloading
explanation: This concept demonstrates how C++ allows defining function templates with multiple type parameters to create generic, type-independent functions. Specifically, it shows overloading an operator (in this case, 'operator>') for custom iterator types, enabling comparisons between reverse iterators instantiated with different underlying iterator types. This approach promotes code reuse, flexibility, and type safety in generic programming, especially within the context of the Standard Template Library (STL).
syntax:
template <class Type1, class Type2>
bool operator>(const reverse_iterator<Type1>& x, const reverse_iterator<Type2>& y);
example_explanation: This example defines a template function that overloads the 'operator>' for comparing two reverse iterators with potentially different underlying iterator types. In 'main', it creates reverse iterators from two vectors and uses the overloaded operator to compare them. The example demonstrates how C++ templates enable writing flexible, type-agnostic functions that work seamlessly with STL iterators, illustrating advanced template programming and operator overloading in modern C++.
